title: Motorcycle Collision
content:
09.06.26
On June 8, 2026, at approximately 6:01 p.m., members of the Medicine Hat Police Service (MHPS), along with emergency services, responded to a single-vehicle collision involving a motorcycle on the eastbound lanes of the Trans-Canada Highway near Redcliff.
Initial investigation indicates the rider was travelling eastbound when they lost control of the motorcycle and entered the ditch separating the eastbound and westbound lanes. The motorcycle travelled in the ditch for approximately 350 feet before coming to a stop.

Police established containment of the area and conducted a search of the property. During the search, officers located a male suspect hiding beside the garage. When advised he was under arrest, the male fled on foot.

Resist arrest
The accused was transported to the Medicine Hat Police Service and held for a judicial interim release hearing. He was later released and is scheduled to appear in Medicine Hat Provincial Court on June 18, 2026.

title: Fraud in Progress – Firearm Seized
content:
09.06.26
On June 7, 2026, at approximately 11:42 p.m., members of the Medicine Hat Police Service responded to a report of a theft in progress at a restaurant in the 2500 block of Box Springs Boulevard NW. Two individuals allegedly left without paying for their meal.
Police arrived shortly afterward and located one adult female inside the establishment attempting to address the outstanding bill. The second male individual was located a short time later inside the restaurant and was taken into custody without incident.
During the arrest, officers recovered a backpack belonging to the male individual. A search incidental to arrest resulted in the seizure of a loaded .22 calibre rifle that had been modified, along with ammunition. The firearm was concealed within a carrying case inside the backpack.
Subsequent investigation revealed both individuals were bound by existing court-imposed conditions and were in breach of those conditions at the time of the incident. One individual was also found to be in possession of identification belonging to another person.
Resulting from this investigation, Jade Holt, age 26, of Medicine Hat, was charged with the following:
Failure to comply with a release order (4 counts)
Food fraud
Possession of identity documents
Connor Brace, age 22, of Medicine Hat, was charged with the following:
Breach of probation order (3 counts)
Possession of a prohibited / restricted firearm contrary to a court order
Carrying a concealed weapon
Careless storage of a firearm
Possession of a weapon for a dangerous purpose
Unauthorized possession of a firearm
Food fraud
Possession of a restricted firearm without a licence
Possession of a loaded prohibited / restricted firearm
Both individuals were held for judicial interim release hearings and remanded into custody pending their next court appearance in Medicine Hat Provincial Court on June 9, 2026.

title: Flight from Police
content:
17.06.26
On June 15, 2026, the Medicine Hat Police Service received a report of a stolen vehicle in the Southeast Hill area. Officers found the vehicle shortly afterward, but when they attempted a traffic stop, the driver fled at a high rate of speed. For public safety reasons, officers did not pursue the vehicle.
Later that day, officers responded to an unrelated call downtown and encountered the same individual believed to be connected to the earlier stolen vehicle incident. When officers attempted to arrest him, he fled on foot and entered the South Saskatchewan River to evade arrest.
With the assistance of a MHPS Police Service Dog Unit (K9), officers safely apprehended the individual and removed him from the river. Despite being taken from the water, the individual continued to resist arrest and made further attempts to flee before being taken into custody.
Brenden Carey, 27, of Medicine Hat, faces the following charges in relation to this incident:
Possession of stolen property over $5,000
Resist arrest
Dangerous driving
Flight from police
Breach of Release Order (2 counts)
Breach of Probation (2 counts)
Carey was held for a judicial interim release hearing where he was remanded into custody until his next court appearance in Medicine Hat Provincial Court on June 17, 2026.

title: High-Risk Incident on Upland Drive SE
content:
25.06.26
On June 24, 2026, at approximately 2:43 p.m., the Medicine Hat Police Service (MHPS) responded to a high-risk incident at a residence in the 1900 block of Upland Drive SE.
When officers arrived, they observed an active physical altercation inside the residence. A victim was safely removed from the home, and officers contained the scene while working to safely take two individuals into custody.
Police negotiators were deployed and contacted an adult male, who exited the residence and was arrested without further incident. The male, 41-year-old Nathan Canfield of Medicine Hat, was charged with the following:
Assault with a weapon
Uttering threats
Breach of probation (4 counts)
A second individual remained barricaded inside the residence and was believed to be in possession of a weapon.
Due to the elevated risk, the MHPS Tactical Arrest and Control Team (TACT) was deployed, and negotiators made several unsuccessful attempts to resolve the situation. After judicial authorization was obtained to enter the residence, officers entered the home at approximately 9:46 p.m. and arrested the second individual, who resisted arrest.
As a result, a 43-year-old male, from Medicine Hat, was charged with the following:
Resisting a peace officer
Breach of a Conditional Supervision Order (x3)
41 Criminal Code charges related to seven outstanding warrants
Both individuals were held for judicial interim release hearings. Canfield was remanded into custody pending his next court appearance on June 29, 2026, in Medicine Hat Provincial Court.
The 43-year-old male, whose name will not be released until the charges are sworn, remains awaiting his judicial interim release hearing. The male sustained minor injuries and was treated at the scene by EMS. No members of the public or MHPS officers were injured during the incident.
The MHPS thanks the public for their cooperation and patience during the incident, which required a significant police presence to maintain public safety.

title: E-Bike Collision Results in Injuries to Two Youths
content:
06.07.26
On July 4, 2026, at approximately 12:55 p.m., members of the Medicine Hat Police Service (MHPS), Medicine Hat Fire and Emergency Services, and Emergency Medical Services (EMS) responded to an injury collision involving a motor vehicle and an e-bike at the intersection of Cameron Road SE and Ross Glen Way SE.
Upon arrival, emergency responders located two youths who had sustained injuries as a result of the collision. Both were transported to hospital for treatment. One of the youths was subsequently transferred to a Calgary hospital with serious, but non-life-threatening, injuries. The driver of the motor vehicle was not injured.
The investigation determined that the driver of the vehicle had come to a complete stop at the posted stop sign and had begun making a right turn onto Cameron Road SE when an e-bike carrying two youths entered the intersection from the sidewalk at a high rate of speed and rode into the path of the vehicle.
Investigators also determined that neither youth was wearing a bicycle helmet at the time of the collision. The absence of helmets contributed to the severity of the injuries sustained.
Based on the findings of the investigation, no charges are expected to be laid.
The Medicine Hat Police Service would like to remind the public that under Alberta's Vehicle Equipment Regulation, all cyclists and passengers under 18 years of age are required to wear a properly fitted and approved bicycle helmet while riding a bicycle. Riders and passengers of power-assisted bicycles (e-bikes) must wear an approved helmet regardless of age.
Helmets have been proven to significantly reduce the risk of serious head injuries and can play a critical role in preventing life-altering injuries during a collision. MHPS encourages all cyclists and e-bike riders to wear an approved helmet every time they ride and to ensure their helmet is properly fitted and in good condition.

title: MVC Involving Pedestrian

On July 16, 2026, at approximately 7:38 a.m., members of the Medicine Hat Police Service (MHPS), along with Fire Services and EMS, responded to a report of an injury collision involving a pedestrian.
The investigation determined that an 84-year-old male pedestrian was crossing within a marked crosswalk, with the pedestrian crossing signals activated, when he was struck by a pickup truck completing a left turn from southbound 13 Avenue SE onto Southview Drive SE.
The pedestrian was transported by ambulance to hospital and was later airlifted to Calgary for further treatment of serious, life-threatening injuries.
Heavy fog and poor visibility were present in the area during the morning hours and are being considered as factors in this collision.
As a result of the investigation, the driver of the pickup truck has been charged with one count of Failing to Yield to a Pedestrian in a Crosswalk, contrary to Section 41(1) of the Use of Highway and Rules of the Road Regulation and is scheduled to appear in Provincial Court on September 25, 2026. The investigation remains ongoing.
The MHPS reminds motorists to slow down, remain alert, and yield to pedestrians in marked crosswalks. Pedestrians are also encouraged to make eye contact with drivers whenever possible and ensure vehicles have stopped before entering the roadway.

20.07.26
The Medicine Hat Police Service has observed an increase in electric motorcycles being operated in the community. While these vehicles are sometimes mistaken for e-bikes, some electric-powered vehicles may be classified under Alberta legislation as electric motorcycles rather than bicycles.
A vehicle may fall outside the legal definition of an e-bike if it produces more than 500 watts of power, cannot be propelled by muscle power, can exceed 32 km/h, or otherwise does not meet the legal requirements for an e-bike.
Electric motorcycles operated on public roadways must meet the same legal requirements as other motorcycles, including registration, insurance, and the appropriate class of driver’s license. Riders operating an unregistered or uninsured electric motorcycle, or operating without the proper license, may be subject to multiple charges or fines.
These vehicles are also not permitted on multi-use pathways or other areas designated for bicycles. Combined fines and penalties can exceed $4,000.
The Medicine Hat Police Service encourages riders and parents to review the rules for electric-powered vehicles before purchasing or operating them to ensure the vehicle is legal for its intended use.
Stay informed. Stay legal. Stay safe.

title: Shooting Investigation
content:
21.07.26
The Medicine Hat Police Service (MHPS) Major Crimes Unit has charged three individuals following an extensive investigation into a shooting that left a Medicine Hat man with serious injuries. On July 12, 2026, MHPS received a report from Medicine Hat Regional Hospital that a male had arrived with injuries consistent with a gunshot wound. Officers attended the hospital and immediately launched an investigation. Investigators determined the victim had been shot at a residence in the 600 block of 6 Street SW. The victim sustained injuries and underwent treatment to the hospital. Over the course of the investigation, members of the Major Crimes Unit executed search warrants, conducted witness interviews, reviewed extensive CCTV footage, and gathered forensic evidence. Investigators ultimately determined the incident was a targeted attack involving multiple suspects. As a result of the investigation, the following individuals have been charged:
Benjamin Adam, 45, of Medicine Hat has been charged with:
Break and Enter
Aggravated Assault
Assault with a Weapon
Possession of a Weapon Dangerous to the Public Peace
Discharging a Firearm with Intent
Adam is currently in provincial custody, having been sentenced on an unrelated matter following these events. He will be brought before the court pursuant to a judge's order to answer the new charges.
Bodana Dye, 45, of Medicine Hat has been charged with:
Aggravated Assault
Dye was released from custody by a justice of the peace following a bail hearing and is scheduled to appear in court on August 5, 2026.
Jade Holt, 26, of Medicine Hat has been charged with:
Aggravated Assault
Holt was released from custody by a justice of the peace following a bail hearing and is scheduled to appear in court on July 29, 2026.
As this matter is now before the courts, no further details will be released. Anyone with information related to this investigation who has not yet spoken to police is asked to contact the Medicine Hat Police Service at 403-529-8481.

On July 30, 2026, members of the Medicine Hat Police Service Traffic Unit and the Alberta Sheriffs Highway Patrol will conduct joint traffic safety check stops throughout the City of Medicine Hat.

title: Suspended Driver Charged
content:
11.08.26
On August 10, 2026, Medicine Hat Police Service officers were conducting roving patrols in the area of Gershaw Drive SW and the Trans-Canada Highway when they observed a 48-year-old woman operating an e-motorcycle with a wattage greater than 500 watts.
The operator allegedly proceeded through two red lights at a high rate of speed without stopping and narrowly avoided being struck by a transport truck. Officers stopped the operator, who was found to be a suspended driver. She was charged with operating a motor vehicle without insurance, operating a motor vehicle without registration, and failing to stop at a red light.
Police are reminding owners and operators that e-motorcycles and e-bikes with a wattage greater than 500 watts may be classified as motor vehicles. These vehicles require the operator to wear an approved helmet and have valid insurance, registration, and the appropriate class of driver’s licence.

title: Remotely Operated Drone Pilot Program
content:
13.08.26
The Medicine Hat Police Service, in partnership with Skydio, a drone technology provider, is conducting a three-day remotely operated drone pilot program to evaluate the operational feasibility of using drones piloted from police headquarters to support police response.
Over the course of the pilot, a drone will be deployed from the station to support emergency and operational calls for service. MHPS will collect real-world deployment data, response footage, performance metrics, and lessons learned to help inform evidence-based decisions about the potential future implementation of an expanded drone program.
The MHPS is exploring the use of drone technology to determine whether it can enhance community and officer safety by providing timely, up-to-date information that helps guide a safe and effective response to calls for service.
Community safety, privacy, and responsible use remain central to this pilot. Drone deployments will be conducted in accordance with applicable laws, regulations, and MHPS policies, and the technology will be used only to support public safety operations. Any information collected during the pilot will be managed in accordance with applicable privacy legislation and MHPS policies.
At the conclusion of the pilot on August 14, 2026, MHPS will review the findings and assess whether remotely operated drone technology could responsibly support future police operations.
